#EDA 


```{r}
#EDA of total revenue for appliances and electronics
total_rev = aggregate(revenue ~ category, data = walmart, FUN = sum)

barplot(total_rev$revenue,
        names.arg = total_rev$category,
        col = c("purple", "red"),
        main = "Total Revenue by Category",
        ylab = "Total Revenue")

boxplot(revenue ~ category,
        data = walmart,
        col = c("purple", "red"),
        main = "Revenue per Transaction by Category",
        ylab = "Revenue per Transaction",
        xlab = "Category")

boxplot(quantity_sold ~ category,
        data = walmart,
        col = c("purple", "red"),
        main = "Quantity Sold by Category",
        ylab = "Quantity Sold")

boxplot(customer_age ~ category,
        data = walmart,
        col = c("purple", "red"),
        main = "Customer Age by Category",
        ylab = "Customer Age")

ggplot(walmart, aes(x = category, fill = customer_gender)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  labs(title = "Gender Distribution by Category",
       x = "Category",
       y = "Number of Transactions",
       fill = "Gender")
```
The data looks very similar across all of the plots. 

```{r}
t.test(revenue ~ category, data = walmart)

t.test(quantity_sold ~ category, data = walmart)

t.test(customer_age ~ category, data = walmart)

```

the t-tests were used to show any sigificant differences in unit_price,quantity sold, customer age, and revenue within the the two categories and they all seem to fail to reject the null hypothesis. There isn't a difference in all four tests.


```{r}

contable_gender = table(walmart$category, walmart$customer_gender)
chisq.test(contable_gender)

```

similarily, the chi-square test didn't show a disparity between genders as sales seem to be the same among genders.

```
